title: Lemna minor sterilization
author: Jason Laurich
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9gdh3s6

steps.title: Initial Surface Rinse
steps.instruction: Strain duckweed plants in a tea-strainer under running water to remove surface algae.

steps.title: Initial PBS Wash
steps.instruction: Transfer surface-rinsed duckweed into a water bath, then move up to 50 plants into a 50 mL Falcon tube approximately half full of autoclaved Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS).

substeps.instruction: Vortex or shake the tube intensely for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Bleach Sterilization
steps.instruction: Perform the following steps within a safety cabinet: strain plants into a tea-strainer reserved for bleaching, dislodging any plants stuck to the Falcon tube walls with distilled water.

substeps.instruction: Place plants in 1% sodium hypochlorite bleach for 60 seconds.

steps.title: Rinse and Decontaminate
steps.instruction: Remove plants from bleach and rinse the tea-strainer thoroughly by moving it around in a jar of autoclaved distilled water.

substeps.instruction: Soak plants in autoclaved distilled water for 5 minutes or more.
Repeat the soak 3 times, using a new jar of fresh autoclaved distilled water for each rinse.

steps.title: Initial Recovery
steps.instruction: Open the tea-strainer and pour autoclaved medium (e.g., Hoagland's or Krajncic medium) over the plants to dislodge them into a clean, autoclaved jar (e.g., 500 mL Mason jar).

substeps.instruction: Seal the jar with a lid.
Move the jar to an environmental chamber.
Wait at least 3 days for the plants to recover from bleaching.

steps.title: Transfer to Enriched Media
steps.instruction: In a safety cabinet or other sterile location, transfer plants to an autoclaved Mason jar approximately half full of enriched media.

substeps.instruction: Prepare enriched media by adding 1 g yeast extract and 10 g sucrose per L.

steps.title: Contamination Check and Remediation
steps.instruction: Monitor the media for 2-3 days for opacity, which indicates bacterial contamination.

substeps.instruction: If media is cloudy: wash plants and transfer to a Mason jar with autoclaved, unenriched media in a safety cabinet.
Wait one week or more for plants to recover (look green and healthy), then re-sterilize if necessary until all bacteria are removed.
